Great price, poor quality. I used 14 of these to control 40 20A circuits on one timer. 5 stars for the price/value and 2 stars for the quality. these have real fragile plastic covers and we had a few damaged in shipping, one was shattered and unusable. Order 10% extra if you need to do a bunch. Out of the box all of the contacts have 1/4” blades for quick connectors, which I only trusted to carry the small current of the control circuit. I snapped them off of the load and line terminals by twisting them in the flat jaws of my lineman’s pliers, then loosened the screws, then pried up the top brass plate on each side of each screw with a 1/8” wide flathead screwdriver to give me enough room to fit stranded 12G THHN wire. The load/line screws can be tightened with a 5/16” nut driver bit or a Phillips#3. Don’t use an impact driver or you can easily over tighten and strip the threads the screws tighten onto. Use a regular old drill/driver with the torque setting on 15 or whatever is high on yours, or use a screwdriver. These were a great inexpensive option for lighting control in our flowering room of our cannabis grow. If I was on the job I’d never use this cheap crap, any inspector would laugh at and fail me, but for our growing hobby it saved a couple grand over UL listed lighting controls. If we start making any money and hire employees, I’ll re-do them with UL listed parts for liability of course, but they’re safe enough for me and my buddies for now.

Maybe some people can get this to work but I was not one of them... (READ UPDATE). This is a kit. A tinkerer's model. For those people this might be a good purchase....maybe. All I can say is that I've had it for a week and after countless YouTube videos and reading message boards I'm no closer to getting a print that works than I was before I got the Ender 3. The endless series of settings and fiddly bits that can go wrong are too many to count. I just spent 6 hours today trying to get the bed level. It's insane. There are a bazzilion, mods and attachments that are supposed to make this better. In my humble opinion, none of them work. Maybe the mods that you can print are good, but since I can't get the printer to give me a print...well I can't tell you. The only reason I'm giving it two stars is that I know people swear by this printer. I know that honest people say this a great printer for the price and beyond. It's just my experience that this is not the case. If you are considering this printer and are anything less than a serious, and I mean serious, hobbyist, I would probably recommend that you wait however long you need to save a little extra something else. You'll save yourself a hassle, time and probably a little bit of your sanity. UPDATE : OK! So after some help from the folks at Creality and some online help I've gotten the Ender to print very well. I've cranked out a lot of models since the calibrations and it's 95% good. (There's always a little something). That all said, I would say that you do need a bit of patience and a learning curve to get all the settings dialed in. My biggest problem was the assembly of the machine. I probably needed to do a better job. So if you can get it dialed in this is a great printer at this price...and now that I've done it it's not as hard as it seemed a month ago. There are A LOT of resources online for help and don't hesitate to contact Creatlity Support. I've found them very responsive and helpful, willing to stick with me as we solved some problems. All that's needed is time, patience and perseverance. Cheers.

Can't transition even very small bumps with mop attactment. I've been running Neato vacs for a while, but they have gotten tiresome because of all the pre-cleaning I have to do. According to all the reviews and videos I had seen online, this should have solved my issues with better obstacle avoidance, etc. However, it can't traverse even the smallest of changes in floor surface with the mop attached. It gets hung up on area rugs, and even thresholds. I've attached a couple of photos of a place it is getting "trapped". As you can see, it is a very small transition from an area rug to wooden floor and the robot just can't handle it. The tech is very cool....When you do "untrap" it, the bot finds its position and resumes (much better than the Neato vacs which would just fail at that point). The features are neat, the app is great. That's why I'm giving it 2 stars instead of just one. If you have all hardwood, I'm sure this would be a really nice vac. But it needs to be able to step over a 1/8" high rug transition without getting stuck. EDIT: I've added a star to this. Roborock support reached out to me about this review and was very eager to assist. Good support deserves credit for sure. They have asked about the fan it got stuck on and wanted pictures. Also, they suggest that I remove the mop as the robot can only do 4mm high carpet with the mop attached (I never saw that number anywhwere). They say it can do 20mm with the mop off, although I haven't yet tried it, and they suggest making no mop zones in the app. EDIT2: Support continued to reach out to make sure things were better. Things were much improved after my initial run. You do need to spend some quality time with the app to tweak the map, but once you do, it gets much better. I was hoping I would seamlessly transition between mop and vacuum, but that isn't going to be the case because of the aforementioned issue, so I'm capping it at 4 stars. I'm sure the new S7 MaxV Ultra Mark 2 (joking) will fix this.
